# larm_monitor (Resource)

Manages a Larm monitor. The `config` attribute is polymorphic per `check_type` — use `jsonencode({...})` to pass the configuration map.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "larm_monitor" "homepage" {
  name       = "Homepage"
  check_type = "http"

  config = jsonencode({
    url                   = "https://larm.dev"
    method                = "GET"
    expected_status_codes = [200]
    follow_redirects      = true
  })
}

resource "larm_monitor" "cron" {
  name       = "Nightly batch"
  check_type = "heartbeat"

  config = jsonencode({
    expected_interval  = 86400
    consecutive_misses = 1
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `check_type` (String) Type of check. One of `http`, `tcp`, `dns`, `heartbeat`, `synthetic`. Changing this forces replacement.
- `config` (String) Check-type-specific configuration as a JSON-encoded string. Use `jsonencode({...})`. Compared semantically, so formatting differences do not produce diffs.
- `name` (String) Human-readable monitor name.

### Optional

- `alert_channel_ids` (Set of String) IDs of alert channels notified for this monitor.
- `confirm_down_after` (Number) Consecutive failed runs a synthetic monitor needs before going DOWN.
- `confirm_down_minutes` (Number) Minutes a non-synthetic monitor must be failing before going DOWN.
- `confirm_up_after` (Number) Consecutive passed runs a synthetic monitor needs before going UP.
- `confirm_up_minutes` (Number) Minutes a non-synthetic monitor must be passing before going UP.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the monitor is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
- `interval_seconds` (Number) Seconds between checks. Defaults to `180`.
- `timeout_ms` (Number) Per-check timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to `10000`.

### Read-Only

- `current_state` (String) Current evaluator state. One of `pending`, `up`, `down`, `degraded`, `stale`.
- `heartbeat_token` (String, Sensitive) Server-generated heartbeat token. Only present for `heartbeat` monitors.
- `id` (String) Monitor ID.
- `inserted_at` (String) RFC3339 creation timestamp.
- `updated_at` (String) RFC3339 last-update timestamp.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import larm_monitor.homepage 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
